newsitem.title: THAILAND: Market talk says Thai central bank chief may quit.
newsitem.headline: Market talk says Thai central bank chief may quit.

text.p: Rumours circulated in the Thai foreign exchange market on Thursday that central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond would resign, dealers said.

But central bank officials were not available to confirm or deny the talk which followed reports in some small Thai business newspapers that Rerngchai might have prepared his resignation letter and could submit it to the finance minister later on Thursday. The Thai baht dropped on the rumours.
The baht fell to 25.960/965 against the dollar on Thursday from around 25.945/950 late on Wednesday on the rumour, dealers said.
Rerngchai was not available for comment but an official in his office told Reuters that he came to office as usual, was meeting other bank officials and she detected no signs he might quit.

The newspaper reports speculated that Rerngchai might resign in protest against the government's suspension of three Bank of Thailand officials, including deputy governor Jaroong Nookhwun, on Wednesday.

The officials were suspended in connection with their failure to bring former executives of the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce to court for violations of the Banking Act, a government spokesman said. Prosecutors last month said they were forced to drop charges against the executives because a one-year statute of limitations had expired.
